events.text: A herald in the colours of a pantheon you owe comes to your temple and does not sit down. "It is time," the herald says. "You know what was promised. We would like it now, or we would like a reason."

choices.text: Go yourself and do what it asks

effects.log: You go where you are asked and do what is asked, and come back tired.
You send the faith of a hundred temples in your place.
You send the herald back with nothing but your refusal.

events.text: A tablet of light arrives at the door of your domain, very short and very polite, which is how you know it is serious. A pantheon you owe has decided the debt is due. Its sigil is at the bottom, beside yours, from long ago.

choices.text: Go yourself and do what it asks

effects.log: You go where you are asked and do what is asked, and come back tired.
You send the faith of a hundred temples in your place.
You send the herald back with nothing but your refusal.

events.text: At the feast of the gods a god of a pantheon you owe leans across the table and says, pleasantly, that their hall has a small task and a long memory, and that the two have met.

choices.text: Go yourself and do what it asks

effects.log: You go where you are asked and do what is asked, and come back tired.
You send the faith of a hundred temples in your place.
You send the herald back with nothing but your refusal.

events.text: Every five years the heralds of your pantheon and of its old rival carry lamps against each other across a field of cloud, three a side, until one side's lamps are all out. The heralds of your hall are choosing who will carry this year's.

effects.log: You take a lamp and step onto the field of cloud.
You watch from the seats with the rest of the hall.

events.text: The Contest of Lamps comes round again. The rival pantheon's three heralds are already on the field of cloud, lamps lit, and the gods of both halls are finding their seats. A place in your line is still open.

effects.log: You take a lamp and step onto the field of cloud.
You watch from the seats with the rest of the hall.

events.text: The elders of your hall want the Contest of Lamps won this time; the rival pantheon has carried it twice. A herald asks you, carefully, whether you would carry a lamp, since you are still among the heralds.

effects.log: You take a lamp and step onto the field of cloud.
You watch from the seats with the rest of the hall.

events.text: A god of the pantheon you remember sits down beside you at the feast and says, very quietly, "You knew which way the vote would go before it was called. You knew my name before we met. How?"

choices.text: Tell them some of the truth

effects.log: You tell them a little. They listen, and remember every word.
You smile and say nothing, and it is very nearly enough.

events.text: A herald of the hall you remember follows you for three domains and then simply asks: how does a god so new know the old corridors of their hall, and which doors are false?

choices.text: Tell them some of the truth

effects.log: You tell them a little. They listen, and remember every word.
You smile and say nothing, and it is very nearly enough.

events.text: An elder god you remember from another life looks at you for a long time across the hall. "You look at me," they say, "as if you know how I end. Do you?"

choices.text: Tell them some of the truth

effects.log: You tell them a little. They listen, and remember every word.
You smile and say nothing, and it is very nearly enough.

events.text: You find it at last: the domain that was yours in another life. Its temples are cold, its valleys grey, and the few worshippers left pray to a name that is not yours and get no answer. Something sits on its throne that was never its god.

effects.log: You walk in, and a single lamp in the first temple lights itself as you pass.

choices.text: Leave it: it was another life

effects.log: You leave it to whoever sits there.

events.text: A pilgrim tells you of a domain where the lamps have gone out and the priests pray to an empty throne. When you hear its name you know it before you know why. It was yours, once, a life ago.

choices.text: Go and see it with your own eyes

effects.log: You go. It is worse than the pilgrim said, and it is still yours.

choices.text: Let the pilgrim's story go by

effects.log: You let it go by. Another life, another domain.

events.text: The temples of your fallen domain have to be lit again before its worshippers will believe. Each lamp asks for faith, or for a god patient enough to sit with the priests until they remember what they were praying for.

choices.text: Pour your own faith into the lamps

effects.log: You pour it in, temple by temple, all the way down the valley.

choices.text: Sit with the priests until they remember

ok.log: They remember. One by one, the lamps take light from yours.

fail.log: They do not remember yet. You will have to come back.

events.text: The old priests of the fallen domain have kept one hymn to you, half wrong, in a cellar under the cold temple. They sing it for you, badly, and look at you to see whether you are the one it was for.

choices.text: Sing it back to them, right

ok.log: You sing it back to them the way it was. The old priests weep, and the lamps light.

fail.log: You do not remember it all either. The priests are kind about it.

choices.text: Light the lamps with your faith instead

effects.log: You light them with faith. The priests do not need the hymn after that.

events.text: Now the usurper on the throne of your old domain knows you are here. It comes down the temple steps to meet you, wearing a stolen crown of light, and says the domain has forgotten you. The lamps behind you say otherwise.

ok.log: The usurper goes down on the steps.

fail.log: The usurper holds the throne this time. The lamps you lit stay lit.

choices.text: Leave it to the usurper after all

effects.log: You turn back at the foot of the steps.

events.text: The usurper of your old domain does not come down to meet you. It waits on the throne, as if the throne made it a god, and the worshippers stand between you, not knowing which of you to pray to.

ok.log: The worshippers know which one to pray to by the time you reach the top.

fail.log: The usurper keeps the throne, this year. The worshippers keep looking at you.

effects.log: You go. The worshippers watch you leave.
